subject: Post-demo: RAG evaluation checklist, model recommendations, and retrieval tuning
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@summithealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@summithealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — next steps

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough today — the demo gave us a good sense of how Redwood's RAG approach could fit into our clinician-facing knowledge assistant. A few tidy notes from our side and requests to help us qualify fit: 

- Can you send recommended model families (and quantization profiles) you think are a good starting point for hospital policies + clinical safety?
- We want to run a quick quality benchmark against our curated KB (approx 250k docs). Can you share a sample prompt set and a short checklist for retrieval + reranker config we should evaluate?
- Any concerns about hallucination/factuality metrics for clinical content? We need measurable pass/fail criteria for our internal review.

Also looping in Priya (security & procurement). We may need a short note on retention/KMS for the eval environment.

Would appreciate the artifacts and a short proposed timeline so we can align with our compliance review.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Clinical Informatics
Summit Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@summithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps

Samir — great meeting, appreciate the clear asks. Per below is a concise post-call recap and an actionable evaluation plan. I attached the prompt set (prompt-set-v1.csv) and a short benchmark summary (.pdf). Also recording attached.

Post-call recap (high level):
- Goal: 2-week RAG proof-of-concept to validate grounding and precision on clinician Q&A with our KB (~250k docs).
- Success criteria we propose: precision@3 >= 85% (clinically accurate answers), hallucination incidents <= 3% on sampled queries, median latency < 500ms for end-to-end (retrieve + rerank + generation) under 90th pct traffic.

Recommended model families (starting presets):
- Candidate A (high-fidelity, lower cost): flan-t5-xl (decoder-encoder ensemble for concise clinical answers) — run int8 quantized.
- Candidate B (strong contextual reasoning): open-llama-30b-int8 (we recommend 30B int8 for higher hallucination resilience on long contexts).
- Candidate C (fast, iter-friendly): redwood-inference/commandant-7b-q4 (good throughput for iterative prompt tuning).

Retrieval & reranker baseline (what to evaluate):
- Retriever: BM25 (index all docs chunked at 512 tokens, overlap 64). Suggest top_k_retrieve = 100 for initial pass to maximize recall.
- Vector store: FAISS IVF-PQ fallback in our hosted eval (we'll provide snapshot of indexed vectors).
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker (MS-MARCO fine-tuned or equivalent) to score top_k_retrieve down to top_k_final = 10. We recommend testing both a sentence-transformer dual-encoder (fast) and a cross-encoder (higher quality) to trade off cost/latency.
- Generation: use constrained decoding with entity filters and hallucination penalty tokens (we'll supply prompt templates).

Proposed evaluation artifacts I attached:
- prompt-set-v1.csv — 120 clinician queries broken down by intent (diagnosis, protocol lookup, drug interactions, local policy).
- benchmark-summary.pdf — suggested metrics, scoring rubric, and an initial dashboard mock.
- summit_demo-recording.mp4 — recording from today's demo.

Evaluation plan & timeline (suggested):
- Day 0–2: Provide data snapshot + access (we'll share indexing script; need S3 access or upload to our eval bucket).
- Day 3–7: Indexing + baseline retrieval configs (BM25 + initial vector index) + run candidate A/B/C without reranking to measure recall/latency.
- Day 8–11: Run reranker experiments (cross-encoder vs dual-encoder) and generation pass.
- Day 12–14: Manual review + metric calculation, produce pass/fail and go/no-go recommendation.

Action items (owner):
- Summit: provide data snapshot and a sample of redaction rules (Samir, Priya) — due Day 1.
- Redwood: deliver prompt set + indexing scripts + initial benchmark run (Vanessa) — due Day 3.
- Security sync: set up a short call to confirm retention/KMS for the eval env (Marissa to lead).

Security & retention notes:
- For the eval we can spin up a private eval bucket with customer-managed KMS. Data retention can be set to 30 days by default; we can mirror your retention policy. We'll provide an evidence pack (SOC2 checklist items) for your security review.

If that looks good I can schedule the 30-minute kickoff with engineering (Dylan) and Marissa for security on Monday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@summithealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@summithealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps

Thanks Vanessa — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick security/procurement questions before we kick off: 

1) For the eval bucket + KMS, can you confirm whether keys are customer-managed (we require CMK) and whether access logs (S3 access logs / CloudTrail) will be retained for 90 days?
2) Will the eval environment support a temporary, scoped service account for indexing so we don't need to share long-lived credentials?

If both are yes, we can sign off on providing a data snapshot and move to Day 0.

—Priya
Sr. Manager, Vendor Security & Procurement
Summit Health
